# NetworkManager OpenVPN 3 SSO Plugin

> A NetworkManager VPN plugin that drives the OpenVPN 3 Linux client with browser-based Single Sign-On (SSO).

This plugin activates VPN connections through the OpenVPN 3 Linux D-Bus services (configuration manager, session manager, netcfg) instead of spawning an `openvpn` 2.x process. When the server demands web authentication, the plugin opens the user's browser (via `xdg-desktop-portal`, falling back to `xdg-open` as the desktop user); after the login — including any second factor at the identity provider — the OpenVPN 3 backend completes the handshake by itself.

## Links

- [Documentation](https://code-acrobat.github.io/network-manager-openvpn3-sso/)
- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/code-acrobat/network-manager-openvpn3-sso)

## Key Features

- OpenVPN 3 Linux backend (no openvpn 2.x process; requires openvpn3-linux ≥ 20)
- Browser-based SSO authentication with second-factor support
- Profile synthesis: works with intact `.ovpn` files and with the fragment form `nmcli connection import` produces
- NetworkManager-aware IP config: relays tunnel address/prefix/gateway and marks the tunnel `never-default` so NM does not hijack the default route or DNS
- Native KDE Plasma plasma-nm UI plugin (from the upstream project)
- Packages for Arch Linux, Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora/RHEL, and generic Linux tarballs

## Installation

```bash
# Arch Linux
sudo pacman -U networkmanager-openvpn3-sso-*-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst

# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt install ./networkmanager-openvpn3-sso_*_amd64.deb

# From source
git clone https://github.com/code-acrobat/network-manager-openvpn3-sso.git
cd network-manager-openvpn3-sso
cargo build --release
sudo ./install.sh
```

## Quick Start

```bash
# Import an OpenVPN configuration
nmcli connection import type openvpn file your-vpn-config.ovpn

# Switch the connection to use the SSO plugin
nmcli connection modify "your-vpn-name" vpn.service-type org.freedesktop.NetworkManager.openvpn3-sso

# Connect (browser opens for SSO authentication)
nmcli connection up "your-vpn-name"
```

## Notes

- openvpn3's netcfg owns the tun device, routes and DNS; the plugin only reports the resulting configuration to NetworkManager.
- Logs: `journalctl -t nm-openvpn3-sso-service -f`
- Hard fork of `quinnjr/network-manager-openvpn-sso` with thanks to Joseph R. Quinn for the original plugin and the Plasma UI. MIT License.
